https://www.politico.eu/article/russia-c.text: The European Union has collected €1.4 billion in revenue from immobilized Russian central bank assets and will channel the proceeds to Ukraine, the European Commission announced Wednesday. In a press release , the Commission said the payment, received Monday, was the “fifth transfer of its kind.” Since the assets have been immobilized, they have generated a total of €8 billion in windfall profits. Brussels said 95 percent of the latest tranche would go through the Ukraine Loan Cooperation Mechanism, helping Kyiv repay EU and G7 loans, while the remaining 5 percent would flow through the European Peace Facility to meet Ukraine’s “pressing military and defence needs.” Advertisement Advertisement “Once again we wake up to the news of horrible atrocities by Russia through its aerial attacks on Ukraine,” Commission President Ursula von der Leyen wrote on X. “Russia must pay for the destruction it has caused. And we are using the proceeds from the immobilised Russian assets to make sure it does.” Von der Leyen said the EU was making “a further €1.4 billion” available to support Ukraine’s “continued resistance against Russia’s illegal war.” Her comments came after one of the deadliest Russian attacks on Kyiv this year. Ballistic missiles and drones killed at least 17 people and wounded 44 overnight, striking residential buildings, warehouses and a railway station. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated Wednesday that additional missile interceptors “could have saved lives” and blamed delays in Western air-defense deliveries for the mounting casualties. Over €210 billion in Russian central bank reserves were frozen by the EU after Moscow’s full-scale invasion in 2022. Since 2024, financial institutions holding those assets have been required to ring-fence the extraordinary profits they generate, allowing Brussels to redirect the proceeds to Ukraine while leaving the underlying reserves untouched.

France welcomes Leo XIV at Orly Airport as bells sound nationwide Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 25/09/2026 - 12:20 GMT+2 Pope Leo XIV begins historic four-day visit to France with focus on Europe’s future. … More President Emmanuel Macron welcomed the Pope on his arrival at around 10am, before military honours and introductions to French and Vatican officials. The two then made their way to the Élysée Palace for talks. ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT The four-day visit , running from Friday to Monday, will take the Pope to Paris, Saint-Denis, Lourdes and Metz . His programme includes meetings with Macron, French officials, civil-society representatives and diplomats, as well as a visit to UNESCO and meetings with young Catholics . The agenda is expected to include the future of Europe, social issues and the role of technology, including artificial intelligence, although the published programme does not explicitly list AI as a formal agenda item. Church bells rang across France for seven minutes to mark the Pope’s arrival, including at Notre-Dame Cathedral in Paris and churches in cities such as Lourdes, Marseille, Lyon and Orléans. Leo XIV’s visit is the first official papal state visit to France since Pope Benedict XVI travelled there in September 2008. On Friday evening, Leo XIV is due to attend a prayer vigil with young people aged between 17 and 35 at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis. Organisers expect around 80,000 participants . His itinerary will then continue with a mass in Paris, followed by visits to Lourdes and Metz , where he is scheduled to address the theme “At the roots of Europe for peace and unity”. https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/in.text: EU Calls for European Security Council in New Defense Plan September 17, 2026 by Jorge Valero and Andrea Palasciano The European Union proposed creating a security structure with like-minded allies to confront growing threats amid doubts about President Donald Trump’s commitment toward the North Atlantic Treaty Organization. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen floated a so-called European Security Council during her state of the union address in Strasbourg, France, Wednesday. “Europe needs its own counter-hybrid playbook. We urgently need a consensus on how to respond to certain incidents,” Von der Leyen said. “The urgency is clear. And the principle is simple: Europe’s security is indivisible.” Read more: Russia’s Attacks on Europe Are Getting More Brazen and More Dangerous The plan would create an emergency security protocol that, when triggered by member states, would activate all countries to convene and coordinate a European response. It would also create a format focused on security with partners like Ukraine, the UK, Norway and Canada. The initiative comes as Europe grapples with a shifting geopolitical climate over the past few years as the US has threatened to pull back from NATO and China has become an increasingly important global player. France and other member states have supported pan-European initiatives to regain control on security matters, including a European Security Council. The EU’s defense chief, Andrius Kubilius, has also been calling for setting up such format. But the idea, which could group nations like UK, Ukraine or Canada, would clash with US-led NATO, the main provider of security for the continent. NATO has long bristled at what they perceive as the EU duplicating its structures without the actual war-fighting competences and procedures to back it up. “Can we seriously afford to spend time, money and energy creating an alternative to NATO from scratch — and to do so within an entity that doesn’t even have defense within its remit?,” said Bartosz Grodecki, head of Poland’s National Security Bureau, an advisory body to the country’s president, stressing the increasing risk of Russian escalation in Eastern Europe. “I see this as a purely political declaration.” Photo: Ursula von der Leyen delivers her annual State of the Union address on Sept. 16. https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/externe/ue/m.text: NATO laudă operațiunile Ucrainei împotriva infrastructurii petroliere rusești și susține că loviturile îl afectează direct pe Vladimir Putin. În timp ce oficiali ai Alianței participă la discuțiile de la Abu Dhabi privind viitorul acord de securitate pentru Europa, un comandant NATO spune că rămâne de văzut dacă liderul de la Kremlin este cu adevărat dispus să negocieze pacea. În privința teritoriilor ucrainene, acesta subliniază că decizia aparține exclusiv Kievului, anunță Euronews . Pe măsură ce negocierile menite să pună capăt războiului declanșat de Rusia în Ucraina continuă, NATO este reprezentată la Abu Dhabi de oficiali de rang înalt, printre care se numără și comandantul suprem al Forțelor Aliate din Europa, Alexus Grynkewich. Acesta participă în calitate de comandant al Comandamentului European al SUA, „pentru a oferi consiliere liderilor americani în eforturile acestora de a duce mai departe inițiativele președintelui Trump de a pune capăt războiului dintre Rusia și Ucraina”, au transmis oficialii NATO. Jurnaliștii Euronews au discutat cu adjunctul comandantului suprem al Forțelor Aliate din Europa, John Stringer, la sediul Alianței. Acesta a declarat că speră ca Rusia să participe la negocieri cu bună-credință, dar a subliniat că există puține indicii că Vladimir Putin ar fi renunțat la pretențiile sale maximaliste. Stringer a afirmat că obiectivele Ucrainei în ceea ce privește obținerea unui armistițiu sunt „de o importanță capitală” pentru NATO. „Să vedem cât de serioasă este Rusia în această privință”, a declarat el. „Să sperăm că nu este vorba, sincer, doar despre o reiterare a cererilor care, așa cum am spus, datează din 2022”, a adăugat oficialul, făcând referire la obiectivele inițiale de război ale Moscovei, care includeau și anexarea unor teritorii ucrainene. Întrebat despre temerile că Ucraina ar putea fi presată să accepte modificări ale granițelor sale, inclusiv să renunțe la controlul asupra unor părți din regiunile Donețk și Luhansk, Stringer a subliniat că numai Ucraina poate decide asupra viitorului teritoriului său suveran. „În ceea ce privește teritoriul, decizia aparține în totalitate ucrainenilor”, a spus el. Stringer a lăudat, de asemenea, operațiunile ucrainene care au vizat rafinăriile și infrastructura petrolieră a Rusiei. Președintele american Donald Trump a cerut Kievului să renunțe la această strategie militară, susținând că atacurile contribuie la creșterea prețurilor la energie. Citește și: Kushner și Witkoff la Moscova: SUA vor „binecuvântarea” lui Putin pentru ca Europa să se alăture negocierilor cu Ucraina (Politico) Oficialul NATO a avut însă o poziție diferită și a afirmat că aliații occidentali ar trebui să salute succesele Ucrainei în lovirea infrastructurii rusești și în afectarea capacității lui Putin de a continua războiul. „Acest lucru îl afectează pe Putin. El credea că va putea să invadeze țara și să stabilească o nouă arhitectură de securitate în Europa, începând cu Ucraina, la începutul anului 2022, dar a fost dur dezamăgit în această privință”, a declarat Stringer. „Ceea ce a reușit Ucraina să realizeze prin imaginație, inovație și voință este cu adevărat incredibil și ar trebui să salutăm acest lucru”, a adăugat el.
